sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Belleville?
sections.html:
Belleville is a compact Essex County township of 3.30 square miles of land, and a sale there runs through a township resale certificate, the Essex County Register of Deeds and, for landlords, the township's rent leveling rules. About 56% of homes are owner-occupied, so you will meet both owner-occupant and investor buyers.

The township posts its sale-related forms in one place, which makes it easy to line up paperwork before you list. This page explains those forms, the local numbers and the county and state steps that follow a contract.

sections.h2: How big is Belleville and what do its housing figures show?
sections.html:
Belleville had 38,222 residents in the 2020 census, up from 35,926 in 2010, and the Census Bureau estimates 38,997 for mid-2025. Packed into just over three square miles, that works out to 11,596.5 people per square mile.

The median value of $421,000 and the 2.65 persons per household point to a market of one- and two-family houses on small lots. Ask an agent for sold prices on your own block instead of relying on the township median.

sections.h2: What is Belleville's history and where does it sit in Essex County?
sections.html:
Belleville grew from a settlement called Second River, renamed Belleville in 1797, and it was incorporated as a township in 1839 from part of Bloomfield. The township reincorporated as a town in 1910 and voted to become a township again in 1981. Congress passed a resolution in 1994 recognizing Belleville as the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution in the United States.

The township borders Bloomfield, Newark and Nutley in Essex County, Lyndhurst and North Arlington in Bergen County, and Kearny in Hudson County. The Second River forms much of the border with Newark through Branch Brook Park, and Belleville calls itself the Cherry Blossom Capital of America because of the park's spring display. Silver Lake, split between Belleville and Bloomfield, is the best-known unincorporated community, alongside Belwood, Big Tree and Soho.

The local economy is also worth a line in a listing. Census figures show 68.5% of residents aged 16 and over in the civilian labor force for 2020-2024, retail sales of about $381 million in 2022 and a per capita retail figure of $10,163. Belleville Township spans only 3.37 square miles in total, so most blocks are within a short walk of a bus line or a commercial street.

sections.h2: Which roads, transit and schools help Belleville sell?
sections.html:
Route 7, Route 21 and County Route 506 pass through Belleville, and the Belleville Turnpike Bridge, also called the Rutgers Street Bridge, crosses the Passaic River to North Arlington. The Silver Lake station provides Newark Light Rail service to Newark Penn Station, and NJ Transit buses 13, 27, 72, 74, 90, 92, 93 and 94 run to Newark. The census puts average commute time at 32.4 minutes.

The Belleville School District has 10 schools and 5,095 students in 2023-24, according to Wikipedia's summary of federal data. The township's own links also point residents to Clara Maass Medical Center, and census figures show health care and social assistance receipts of about $807 million in 2022, the largest business total reported for the township.

  • Transit-minded buyers focus on the Silver Lake light rail station and the Newark bus lines.
  • Drivers focus on Routes 7 and 21 and the Turnpike Bridge crossing.
  • Families ask about the Belleville School District, so name it in your listing.

sections.h2: What does the township require before a sale in Belleville?
sections.html:
Belleville posts a Residential Resale Certificate Application and a separate Commercial Resale Certificate application under its Department of Community Development. Ask that office which form fits your property and whether an inspection must happen before you sign a contract.

The same forms page covers other items that come up around a sale, so read through it before you list.

  • Residential Rental Property / New Tenant Certificate Application, plus a Rent Roster form for landlords.
  • Vacant / Abandoned Property Registration, which applies if the house is empty.
  • Request for List of Owners within 200 Feet, used for planning board and zoning board applications.
  • Zoning Permit Application, Fence Permit Application and Pool Permits, which show what work was approved.
  • Landlord Identity Registration Form, filed with the Township Clerk.
  • Fire Department items such as the Fire Safety Permit, a Home Fire Protection Plan and a Fire Safety Checklist for Homeowners and Renters.

Gather the permit paperwork for any work you finished in the house, including fences, pools and driveways, since the township keeps separate applications for each. Having those approvals ready lets a buyer's attorney confirm the work was permitted without waiting on township offices.

sections.h2: How do rent leveling and landlord rules affect a Belleville sale?
sections.html:
Belleville has a Rent Leveling Board, and its forms include a Vacancy Decontrol Application and a Rent Leveling Complaint Form. If you own a rental, check with the board about registration, any open complaints and whether a vacancy decontrol filing is on file before a buyer's attorney asks.

Buyers of tenant-occupied buildings will want copies of leases and the rent roster, so organize them before you list. The township also posts a Continued Certificate of Occupancy form for short-term rentals, which matters if the house was ever rented that way. A clean file shortens attorney review and reduces last-minute price talks.

sections.h2: What property tax and relief records should I gather in Belleville?
sections.html:
Belleville's Tax Assessor page carries a Property Assessment form and a Guide to Appeal Hearings, and the Tax Collector page carries the PD-5 Senior Property Tax Deduction form, a Veteran's Property Tax Credit form and an online payment portal. The township also links the Essex County Board of Taxation and the state's Property Tax Relief Program.

Pull your latest tax bill and any open balance before you list, because buyers and title companies ask for them. If you have a PD-5 deduction or veteran's credit, the buyer will not inherit it automatically, so ask the Tax Collector whether those benefits change after a sale. The township website also lists a Home Improvement Program with an application and a contractor application, which a buyer planning repairs can read.

sections.h2: Where is the deed recorded and what fees apply at closing?
sections.html:
The Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages records the deed, and the Essex County Clerk's site directs callers to the register at 973-621-4960. The seller pays the New Jersey realty transfer fee, and for a deal above $350,000 the state schedule charges $4.80 per $500 on the slice between $200,000 and $550,000.

Some transfers are exempt, including a deed from an executor or administrator to an heir under a will or intestacy and a deed recorded within 90 days of a divorce decree. An estate selling a Belleville house files the state's GIT/REP form according to the estate's residency, and the executor signs it. Ask the title company which forms your closing needs.

faqs.q: Does Belleville require a resale certificate?
faqs.a: The township posts a Residential Resale Certificate Application and a Commercial Resale Certificate application. Ask the Department of Community Development which one applies and when the inspection must occur.

faqs.q: Where is a Belleville deed recorded?
faqs.a: The Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages records it. The county clerk's website lists 973-621-4960 for recording a deed, mortgage or lien.
It has a Rent Leveling Board, with a Vacancy Decontrol Application and a complaint form on the township website. Landlords should confirm their status before selling.

faqs.q: Is a deed from an estate to an heir subject to the realty transfer fee?
faqs.a: No. The state exempts a deed from an executor or administrator to a devisee or heir who receives the property under the will or intestacy. A sale of an estate house to a third party is a normal taxable sale.

faqs.q: How many people live in Belleville?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 38,997 residents as of July 2025, up from 38,222 in the 2020 census. The township covers 3.30 square miles of land.
